rubric.format: JSON Lines, one source-addressed sentence or explicitly labelled prose/table fragment per record
rubric.audience: Mathematically mature reader (mathematics PhD), without assumed specialist physics vocabulary beyond what earlier context teaches.

readability_scale.1: Very difficult: multiple unresolved concepts or opaque structure require reconstruction.
readability_scale.2: Difficult: avoidable jargon, missing bridges, ambiguity or conceptual accumulation forces rereading.
readability_scale.3: Understandable with effort; an avoidable load or transition remains.
readability_scale.4: Clear in context with a small presentational weakness.
readability_scale.5: Easy to follow in context; one coherent explanatory job and established terms.

rigor_scale.1: False or internally inconsistent core claim.
rigor_scale.2: Materially misleading claim, wrong attribution/mechanism, or missing condition that changes the conclusion.
rigor_scale.3: Plausible/mostly correct but scientifically imprecise or missing an important qualification.
rigor_scale.4: Technically sound under stated context; minor qualification or support limitation.
rigor_scale.5: Precise, properly scoped and justified in the supplied context.

rubric.non_claims: Use rigor_score=null and rigor_status=not_applicable only for questions, navigation, pure labels, or instructions that make no scientific assertion. Still assign readability. Actual scientific claims, including empirical claims, need numeric rigor scores.
rubric.rigor_limit: Text-based technical assessment, not an independent literature audit, theorem prover, or experimental verification. Mark empirical/source-dependent uncertainty explicitly; do not pretend citations were checked.
rules: Score semantically, not from sentence length, word counts, jargon dictionaries, or negation regexes.
Assess each sentence with its paragraph, nearby context, section heading and table row supplied. A necessary term taught earlier is not automatically undefined.
Readability and rigor are independent: short false statements can be easy to read; long precise statements can be difficult.
Do not mechanically penalize not/no or scientific comparisons. Penalize empty contrast framing when it obscures explanation.
Every score needs a sentence-specific reason; generic boilerplate is insufficient.
No document rewrites or source edits. Preserve every supplied sentence ID.
Do not invent missing context. Use low confidence and say what is uncertain when necessary.

calibration.text: The Born rule attaches a complex amplitude to each quantum outcome and converts it to a probability through its squared magnitude, generalizing the classical assignment of nonnegative numbers summing to one.
calibration.readability_reason: Introduces amplitudes, outcomes, probability conversion and a classical comparison before resolving any of them.
calibration.rigor_reason: The Born rule gives probabilities from a state and measurement; it does not assign the amplitudes.

calibration.text: The complex conjugate of z is z*=a-ib.
calibration.context: The preceding sentence defines z=a+ib for real a,b.
calibration.reason: One explicit definition using established notation.
Simple wording, but anyons are particles/quasiparticle excitations, not transformations.

calibration.text: A squared magnitude is never negative, so it can serve as a probability.
calibration.reason: The sentence is easy to parse, but a probability also needs normalization and a value at most one.

calibration.text: For U=0, this model has no defect-bound state.
calibration.context: The infinite one-site-defect chain is already defined.
calibration.reason: The negative assertion expresses a precise model limit; it is not empty rhetorical contrast.

extraction.normalization: HTML whitespace normalized; TeX preserved; formula lead-ins and continuations joined before segmentation.
extraction.source_lines: Starting HTML line numbers of constituent blocks, not exact sentence line ranges.
extraction.id_policy: Stable extraction IDs; gaps correspond to 93 excluded Sources-list records.
extraction.included: Main manuscript prose, front matter, notation guide, chapter/part/appendix prose, table entries and figure descriptions.
extraction.excluded: Navigation, headings (context only), bibliographic records, Sources lists and preformatted code. Standalone equations are context, not separately scored prose.
extraction.round_trip: Every non-whitespace character in included passages retained by segmentation.

assessment.method: Contextual semantic assessment by parallel task agents; parent coverage/schema checks and sample review.
assessment.limitations: Ordinal editorial judgments, not objective measurements. Technical rigor assessed from text/context, without independent citation or experimental verification. Nearby context does not guarantee exhaustive review of definitions in all preceding chapters.
assessment.validation: Saved accepted portions passed structural checks and parent samples; not independently reviewed every score. Full-manuscript final integration remains unfinished.

s009105.readability_reason: The dependency sequence is understandable, but grouping disorder and scaling tests under one phrase makes the four-item enumeration less explicit.
s009105.rigor_reason: The four stated steps are mechanism, resulting numbers, disorder tests, and scaling tests. The sentence describes their logical dependency without claiming experimental success; there is no enumeration inconsistency.
